newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour cost index rises 2.5 pct over year.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour cost index rises 2.5 pct over year.

text.p: The New Zealand Labour Cost Index rose by 2.5 percent from the September quarter in 1995 to the September 1996 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
The rise follows increases of 2.1 percent and 2.3 percent in the March and June years.
Labour costs in the public sector in the September year rose 2.6 percent and 2.4 percent in the private sector.
Salary and wage rates rose 1.9 percent and non-wage labour costs rose 4.5 percent, with private sector costs up 4.7 percent and public sector costs up 4.0 percent.
From the June to September quarters labour costs rose 0.7 percent overall, with salary and wage rates rising 0.6 percent and non-wage labour costs increasing by 0.6 percent.
The increase in salary and wage rates, up 1.9 percent, accounted for 68 percent of the 2.5 percent annual increase in labour costs.
An increase in ACC employer premium costs accounted for 19 percent of the latest overall annual increase in labour costs, while leave and holiday costs accounted for 10 percent.
Employee participation in employment-subsidised pension schemes remained steady in the last quarter, halting a downward trend.
